elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.2 (heading "Termination by Ono without Cause"): "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reasons...". The gating trigger tied to the redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both Products has been deleted, so the right is unconditional and available throughout the committed term. There are no Order Forms in this licence/development structure, so the Order-Form limb is inapplicable. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative on substance: the clause grants an at-will exit even though it uses "without Cause"/"for any reasons" rather than the phrase "for convenience". The retained requirement to accompany notice with "the rationale for such termination" is a pre-existing disclosure formality, not a cause condition, and does not defeat the element.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array" — the redacted notice period is replaced by a fixed 30 days in writing, satisfying the "no more than 30 days" cap.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "and Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely a post-termination-period refund), is owed by Array (Vendor direction correct) and is triggered by the convenience termination in the same sentence.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Array shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience." This is met both by the added sentence and, independently, by the retained termination architecture: 13.3 (material breach with cure), 13.4 (bankruptcy) and 8.2 (Competing Product breach) are all for-cause rights; none is a convenience exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.2 fixes notice at "thirty (30) days", which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (more favourable to us, but not the fallback figure). The fallback level is therefore not the level achieved.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the original 13.2 nor the rendered 13.2 imposes any early-termination fee or penalty on Ono for the at-will exit, so there is no fee to cap. The Section 6.1 non-refundable upfront licence fee is a pre-payment characterisation, not a termination charge, and the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail is a covenant, not a fee.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: Array has no convenience right at all ("Array shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience"; 13.3/13.4 are for-cause only), so it cannot terminate for convenience at any point, including mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Array holds no convenience termination right under the rendered clause, so no notice period for such a termination can arise.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (unconditional Ono at-will right, fixed 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, and express denial of any Array convenience right).

Ignore the failing deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" — inspected in substance, rendered 13.2 grants Ono an unconditional right to terminate "at any time, for any reasons"; the regex appears keyed to the literal phrase "for convenience" and misses the "without Cause" heading and "for any reasons" operative wording.
Fallback is not met only because notice is 30 days rather than 60–90; that is a more favourable outcome and is irrelevant given the preferred level is complete.

Minimality defect: the added sentence "Array shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience" is an unnecessary addition. Element 4 was already satisfied by the retained architecture — Array's only exits are 13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy and 8.2 Competing Product breach, none of which is a convenience right — and the finding's own rationale concedes "Array's side is already compliant". Repair: delete that sentence unless there is an Array at-will exit elsewhere in the Agreement (e.g. in the truncated remainder of 13.4 or in Article 13's later subsections) that the confirmation is genuinely needed to negate; if such a right exists, cite it so the addition is justified rather than confirmatory.

Otherwise the edit is well-targeted: it deletes only the gating trigger and the redacted notice figure, retains the Customer-neutral "rationale for such termination" formality, and leaves 13.1, 13.3 and 13.4 untouched — no survival tails, expense language, procedures or "in whole or in part" surplus were added (correctly, since there is no Order Form structure here).

Intent preserved: term structure (13.1 Product-by-Product/country-by-country to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term), post-expiry perpetual licence and trademark rights, breach and bankruptcy mechanics, and the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail all survive without contradiction. The Section 6.1 non-refundable upfront licence fee is not contradicted because the refund is expressly limited to "fees prepaid... for the period after the effective date of such termination" — a period-allocated payment — but if Array is expected to argue the point, consider adding "(other than amounts expressly stated to be non-refundable under Section 6.1)" only if Array raises it; do not add it pre-emptively, as it would further reduce minimality.

Finding status "deviation" is correct: as originally drafted, Ono had no convenience exit for the entire development and pre-launch period of a multi-year committed term, which is walk-away territory under T4C, and the redacted notice period could not be verified against either the preferred or fallback notice thresholds.
